chunks: Therefore, our answer regarding the occultation of the Imam is their answer regarding the prevention of the people of resolution and contract from choosing one suitable for the Imamate, and there is no difference between them, for the only difference between us is that we said: our knowledge of that is through reason, and they said: that is known through Islamic law, and that is a difference from a place of non-union.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْحَلِّ وَالْعَقْدِ: People of resolution and contract (those qualified to choose the leader)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Shia and Sunni views on the necessity of the Imam during the occultation?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi clarifies that the Shia stance on the Imamate during the Major Occultation is structurally identical to the Sunni reliance on the 'ahl al-hall wa-l-'aqd' for selecting a leader, differing only in the source of knowledge. While Sunnis view this selection as a matter of textual legal deduction (shar'), Shias assert it is known through rational necessity ('aql), thereby resolving the apparent epistemological divide. This highlights the Shia doctrine of the Imamate as a rational imperative rather than solely a legislative one.
